corpus.domain: lung disease detection, MLOps + Kafka + FastAPI
corpus.note: The source is NOT committed: it is the user's own personal material, and the provenance rule keeps it out of the repository. Point the env var at the folder before scoring.
corpus.include_note: **/*.py, excluding tests. A real multi-module application: deployment/mlops, deployment/app, deployment/kafka_pipeline, research. ALSO excludes **/mlflow/artifacts/**. Measured 2026-09-18: those 12 files are MLflow RUN ARTIFACTS - the same utils.py copied under a different run hash each time - and they were 330 of 958 chunks (34%), one chunk repeated 16 times. A query anchored to one copy is unanswerable by fair retrieval, because the other 15 identical chunks are equally good answers and score as wrong. 4 of the first 20 drafted queries landed in them. Same class as the fnmatch bug in G1: the include swept in material that is not the authored application.

fields.query: the question, as a developer would ask it
fields.file: the file holding the answer, spelled as Chunk.source spells it
fields.expects: line numbers in that file that answer it
fields.wording: named if it shares ordinary words with the answer, paraphrase if it deliberately avoids them
